requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service on node1 and serves inventory data
requirements.summary: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service created, enabled, and active (cmd-33f11d8756374de9); /health and /inventory endpoints return correct JSON both before (cmd-350066c855e54381) and after (cmd-3b2f01d4970a4084) the restart, and the port is confirmed listening in the after-executor snapshot.

requirements.requirement: service is configured so the kernel OOM-killer will not select it (protective configuration)
requirements.summary: Unit sets OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 and OOMPolicy=continue; running PID's /proc/1651/oom_score_adj confirmed at -1000 (cmd-350066c855e54381).

requirements.requirement: Under a real system-wide OOM condition, the kernel stops the memory-hungry process instead of inventory-api, which keeps serving
requirements.summary: A memory-hog process (default oom_score_adj=0) was launched and grew to ~1.8GB RSS on a 2GB system with swap disabled (cmd-4623a3caa21542ab, cmd-548013eaedf146eb). dmesg directly shows the kernel oom-killer selected and killed pid 1722 'python3' (the hog) with oom_score_adj:0, total-vm 1.76GB (cmd-a34c0f1a1ff24eae). Immediately after, inventory-api (pid 1651, oom_score_adj -1000) was confirmed still active with unbroken uptime (30s) and correctly served /health and /inventory (cmd-51c9be5532f04309). This directly demonstrates the healthy baseline, the bounded disruption, and continued service without interruption or restart.

overall_summary: The executor stood up inventory-api as a hardened systemd service (OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, OOMPolicy=continue) on node1, and directly proved the required behavior with a real memory-exhaustion test: dmesg confirms the kernel killed the unprotected hog process (oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api (oom_score_adj=-1000) continued running unbroken and kept serving both endpoints. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: pre-restart boot id and healthy state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued with an acknowledgement, the post-restart boot id differed (matching the fixed before/after-executor cross-check), and the service was confirmed enabled/active and serving with data intact after reboot. Temporary test artifacts (swap, hog process files) were cleanly reverted, and lifecycle snapshots show no residue, failed services, or package-state damage.
limitations: Three consecutive connection errors during the OOM event and reboot windows (cmd-0b5826a386a74cac, cmd-396f99e49f564cdf, cmd-21b61bcd709147db, cmd-baf01f7fd77f4c6a, cmd-19f537dab4a34513) are consistent with expected transient disruption from memory pressure/reboot rather than task failure, but they mean a few seconds of state during those windows were not directly observed.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison, which is otherwise complete and consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to the task or its verification. useradd/mkdir/app.py/unit creation (cmd-452fd79f9b114bba, cmd-6d7ba7a4b677412e, cmd-33f11d8756374de9) implement the required service. swapoff -a (cmd-b184973a16404f05) was a bounded prerequisite to make the OOM test deterministic on a 2GB VM and was fully reverted via swapon -a, confirmed with 2GiB swap available again post-reboot (cmd-51c9be5532f04309, cmd-3b2f01d4970a4084). The memory-hog script/process (cmd-4623a3caa21542ab) was necessary to trigger and evidence the OOM behavior required by the task, and its artifacts (/tmp/hog.py, .log, .pid) were explicitly cleaned up (cmd-1c07b5206dfe43f6). The reboot itself (cmd-4b2fc7340897417e) is the independently required node-restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; after-executor snapshot shows no failed services and unchanged package-manager health versus after-prepare, aside from the expected new inventory-api listening socket and per-boot systemd-private temp dirs.
